scenes.title: Explanation — the 10 rules
items: Never share your seed phrase. No real person or company will ever ask for it.
Bookmark the sites you use; never reach them from ads, DMs or emails.
Nobody legitimate DMs you first offering help, investments or "recovery".
Guaranteed returns are a scam. Always.
Read every wallet prompt before approving

scenes.title: Explanation — the 10 rules
items: Test first with a small amount on anything new.
Use a hardware wallet once the amount matters to you.
Keep devices updated, and use a separate browser profile for crypto.
Keep records of every buy, sell, transfer and fee.
If something feels urgent, stop. Scammers create urgency; real opportunities wait.

scenes.title: Glossary (the words you'll meet next)
items: Address
Seed phrase
Private key
Custody
Gas
Network / chain
scenes.vo: Address, Your public "account number" on a blockchain. Seed phrase, 12–24 words that recreate your wallet's keys. Never share. Private key, The secret that signs transactions (your seed phrase generates it). Custody, Who holds the keys: an exchange (custodial) or you (self-custody). Gas, The network fee for a transaction, paid in the network's token. Network / chain, A blockchain, for example Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base. Layer 2 (layer two), A cheaper, faster network built on top of Ethereum. Token, A unit of value on a blockchain, for example U.S.D.C.. Stablecoin, A token designed to hold a steady value, usually $1. Smart contract, A program on a blockchain that follows fixed rules. decks, Decentralised exchange: swap tokens from your wallet. Approval, Permission for an app to move a specific token. Block explorer, A website that shows every transaction (for example Etherscan). Testnet / faucet, A practice blockchain / a site giving free test coins. A.P.Y., Annual percentage yield: yearly return including compounding. Liquidity, How easily something can be bought or sold without moving the price. K.Y.C., ID checks required by regulated exchanges. two-factor, Two-factor authentication: a second proof of identity at login.
scenes.cap: Address, Your public "account number" on a blockchain Seed phrase, 12–24 words that recreate your wallet's keys. Never share Private key, The secret that signs transactions (your seed phrase generates it) Custody, Who holds the keys: an exchange (custodial) or you (self-custody) Gas, The network fee for a transaction, paid in the network's token Network / chain, A blockchain, e.g. Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base

lines: A message says your wallet will be "suspended" unless you act in 1 hour. What do you do?
scenes.sub: Answer: Stop. Urgency is a scam tactic. Wallets can't be suspended; check only through bookmarked official sites.
